findings.title: The sendMessage try/catch cannot catch a failed send — pi swallows the rejection, so the documented 'failed send re-arms the run-start reminder' backup never arms
findings.detail: The handler clears the fallback state *before* sending (`compactedSinceUpdate = false; turnsSinceUpdate = 0;` at extensions/todo.ts:448-449) and relies on `catch { compactedSinceUpdate = true; }` (extensions/todo.ts:455-458, comment: "a failed send re-arms the run-start reminder as backup") to cover a failed send. That catch can only see a synchronous throw: pi binds the extension action as `sendMessage: (message, options) => { this.sendCustomMessage(message, options).catch((err) => runner.emitError({ event: "send_message", ... })) }` (node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/core/agent-session.js:2635-2643), and `sendCustomMessage` is `async` (:1697), so a failing append (`_appendCustomMessage` -> `sessionManager.appendCustomMessageEntry`, :1750-1757) rejects that promise instead of throwing into the caller - it becomes a pi extension-error line, not an exception at this call site. Consequence: if the append fails (write error on the session file, or any rejection inside pi's send path), the plan is gone from context, `compactedSinceUpdate` is already false, and `shouldRemind` (extensions/todo.ts:187) stays false until `turnsSinceUpdate >= REMINDER_MIN_TURNS` (4 runs, extensions/todo.ts:39) - the model keeps working on a plan the compaction just removed, with no reminder. The identical wrapper at extensions/recall.ts:1559-1563 means that catch (which logs a 'post-compaction reminder failed' crumb) is equally blind to the failures that can actually happen.
findings.recommendation: Either drop the try/catch and state the behavior honestly, or check the failure through a channel pi actually exposes (the emitError 'send_message' path / a session-manager append that can be verified) before claiming a run-start fallback.

findings.title: Untrusted tool output is copied raw into the judge's prompt, and the judge's verdict then steers the agent in the harness's voice
findings.detail: Still valid; goal.ts is untouched by this diff. `buildSettleJudgeTask` splices `## Digest of the agent's recent work (oldest first, clipped)\n${ctx.workDigest}` verbatim (extensions/goal.ts:854), and the triage twin does the same (extensions/goal.ts:980). `buildWorkDigest` fills that digest from assistant notes, tool-call arguments and tool-result text (cap 6_000 chars), i.e. content untrusted repo files and command output can influence. The only boundary is the agent instruction telling the child to treat the digest as data (SETTLE_JUDGE_AGENT / SETTLE_TRIAGE_AGENT instruction lists), and the verdict is consumed as the harness's own decision (`complete` -> the parent is told to summarize and call `goal complete`, `blocked` -> declare an impasse, `verify`/`continue` drives the settle), so an injected instruction in command output can influence the agent's next step.
findings.recommendation: Fence the digest and previousReason as an explicitly delimited untrusted block (e.g. `<work-digest>…</work-digest>`) and restate the data-only boundary after the block, as well as in the agent instructions.

findings.title: The judge's task — a 6 KB digest of session content, including tool output — is passed to the child as a command-line argument
findings.detail: createLlmSettleJudge passes buildSettleJudgeTask(goal, ctx) as the task argument (goal.ts:894-905); the default runner's defaultSpawn spawns `pi` with buildChildArgs, which appends the task after `--` (args.push("--", task), extensions/subagents.ts:326-345). The task embeds up to WORK_DIGEST_MAX_CHARS (6,000) of session content — assistant notes, the JSON arguments of commands the agent ran (any credential passed inline on a bash command), and their output — so that text is in the process command line for the whole judge timeout, at every turn end, unattended (world-readable /proc/<pid>/cmdline on Linux, and captured by process accounting/EDR/audit logs). Separately, the `idleTimeoutMs: 0` exemption on the same line (the fix that keeps the tool-less judge from being reaped as 'stalled') is not asserted by any test: tests/goal.test.ts:622/:2578/:2645 record only timeoutMs and signal, so dropping it would not fail the suite.
findings.recommendation: Feed the judge/triage task on stdin or a temp file instead of argv (runChild already spawns with stdio ['ignore','pipe','pipe']); at minimum cap the assembled task bytes. Also assert the forwarded `options.idleTimeoutMs === 0` in the judge/triage tests.

findings.title: recall's post-compaction sendMessage failure path is untested
findings.detail: The new session_compact handler wraps pi.sendMessage in a try/catch that logs 'post-compaction reminder failed'. The recall harness's sendMessage (tests/recall.test.ts:144) never rejects and no test overrides it, so the catch branch is dead in the suite. The new test only asserts sent.length === 1 on the success path. A regression that swaps the guard (or that lets the failure propagate and abort the handler before pendingCompact cleanup) would not be caught.
findings.recommendation: Add a test that makes pi.sendMessage throw and asserts the handler does not throw and still completes its cleanup (autoCompactInFlight/pendingCompact reset), since a throwing send must not disturb the compaction bookkeeping.

findings.title: The parent's idle window is a fixed 5m that no longer matches the child's own (configurable) HTTP idle timeout, so a healthy child on a slow local model is still SIGKILLed as a 'dead request'
findings.detail: Still valid. `DEFAULT_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000` (extensions/subagents.ts:38) is what any run that omits `idleTimeoutMs` gets via `resolveIdleTimeoutMs` (extensions/subagents.ts:76-78), and the `subagent` / `subagents` tools pass `parseIdleTimeoutMs(process.env)` (extensions/subagents.ts:962, :1039), whose default is the same constant (extensions/subagents.ts:65-71) — there is no per-task or per-agent override. The child's own HTTP idle timeout is a *user setting* whose default merely happens to be 300_000 and which can be raised or disabled (documented, with `0` disabling, for local models), so on exactly that configuration a child that legitimately streams nothing for >5m inside one LLM wait is SIGKILLed with 'stalled: no output for Ns (request likely dead)'. goal.ts (idleTimeoutMs: 0) and review.ts/scripts/eval-review.ts (their own values) are covered; the subagent delegation tools are the remaining exposure, and the only remedy there is the process-wide `PI_SUBAGENT_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS`, which loosens detection for every child.
findings.recommendation: Derive the default from the run's budget instead of a constant (e.g. `options.idleTimeoutMs ?? Math.min(DEFAULT_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS, Math.max(60_000, timeoutMs / 2))`) and/or add a per-task idle override to taskItem so one slow child can be exempted without loosening every child.

findings.title: parseIdleTimeoutMs still accepts any positive value, so a sub-tick window (2.9, or 300 meant as seconds) SIGKILLs every child on the first tick
findings.detail: Still valid. The positive branch returns the raw number unclamped (`return Number.isFinite(n) && n > 0 ? n : DEFAULT_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS;`, extensions/subagents.ts:70), `resolveIdleTimeoutMs` forwards it unchanged (:76-78), the watchdog only gates on `idleMs > 0` (:646-647) and its tick floor is `Math.max(100, Math.min(5_000, Math.floor(idleMs / 4)))` (:654). Since `lastActivityAt` is initialized at spawn, any window at or below the 100 ms tick kills every child before it can emit its first stdout line, and the caller sees 'stalled: no output for 1s (request likely dead)' with no hint the env value caused it; the values are pinned as correct in tests (`parseIdleTimeoutMs({ PI_SUBAGENT_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS: "1500" }) === 1500`, `"2.9" === 2.9`, tests/subagents.test.ts:325-326). The sibling knob in this repo clamps (`clampInt(env.PI_REVIEW_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS, 5 * 60_000, 10_000, 6 * 60 * 60_000)`, extensions/review.ts:132-136, pinned by tests/review.test.ts).
findings.recommendation: Clamp the positive branch to a sane floor, e.g. `return Number.isFinite(n) && n > 0 ? Math.max(10_000, n) : DEFAULT_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS;`, and update the '2.9'/'1500' expectations so the tests pin the guard.

findings.title: A single lost `tool_execution_end` line latches the new idle watchdog off for the whole run — the dead-request detector fails open
findings.detail: NOT re-raised as an open issue: the code this finding described (`outstandingToolRuns++` / `Math.max(0, ...)` and the unhealed `if (outstandingToolRuns > 0) return;`) no longer exists. The stand-down is now keyed by `toolCallId` in a `Set` (extensions/subagents.ts:519, :555-558), cleared on the next assistant `message_start` (extensions/subagents.ts:559-562) and cleared whenever the stdout cap discards data — the exact loss mechanism the finding identified (extensions/subagents.ts:590-596), with the two heal paths pinned by dedicated tests (tests/subagents.test.ts:683 'heals a lost tool end at the next assistant message_start: the LLM wait is judged again' and :697 're-arms when the stdout cap discards data: the lost lines cannot latch the stand-down'). The diff under review does not touch this code, so nothing reintroduces it.
findings.recommendation: No action needed for this change; keep the automated start/end symbol when the watchdog is next edited.

findings.title: Tests assert the absence of a before_agent_start handler (harness detail) rather than observable behavior
findings.detail: Both new assertions (recall.test.ts:1152 and :2415) check events.get('before_agent_start') === undefined. This asserts a mechanism of the test double — that registerRecallTool never calls pi.on('before_agent_start', …) — not the behavior the change is about (no reminder is injected at run start). Any future refactor that registers a harmless or differently-purposed before_agent_start handler (recall already registers several other events) would fail these tests spuriously, while the tests still would not verify that a run-start injection never reaches the agent.
findings.recommendation: Assert the observable effect instead — e.g. that no message is returned/mutated for the agent at run start — or drop the registration assertion and keep the positive 'reminder is sent at commit' checks.
